answer: No single clerk mints an identity. A key is valid only with 7 of 11 rotating issuers co-signing it, each vetting against a shared atlas of revoked keys. The gate accepts only keys with its quorum; a key with no quorum is rejected, and one compromised node cannot tend the orchard. An issuer signing a duplicate forfeits its $50,000 bond and seat. Bribing a quorum costs about $140,000 per fake against ~$100 per epoch, so break-even takes 1,400 epochs. Every key must cross the ridge of seven signatures first. Bribe seven strangers for one vote, and by morning the quorum has changed.
